units.translation: which the scholiast correctly explains as τοῖς τείχεσι κεκυκλωμέναι [surrounded by the walls]. It is customary to say τεῖχος [a wall] and τάφρον ἐλαύνειν [to drive a ditch] of a wall or ditch being led, examples of which see in Thes. vol. 3 p. 680: but Aeschylus, as Blomfield noted, said ἐληλαμέναι περὶ πύργον [driven around a tower] for περιεληλαμέναι πύργον [driven around a tower], i.e. those around whom a πύργος [tower] has been driven. ἐληλάμεναι [driven] is in M, with the accent added by a later hand, in the copies ἐληλαμέναι [driven] contrary to the rule of the grammarians, on which see Buttmann Gr. Gr. vol. 1 p. 444.
